title: Finance Minister Quiroz outlines economic agenda at Chile Day London 2026 event
text:
Finance Minister Quiroz outlines economic agenda at Chile Day London 2026 event
Finance Minister Jorge Quiroz addressed representatives of the financial sector at Chile Day London 2026, presenting the government's economic agenda aimed at restoring higher levels of growth and investment. The minister highlighted the Capital Market and Home Financing Reform Bill, which is currently under discussion in Congress, as a key component of this strategy on Sep. 16.
"We want to put Chile back in the spotlight. We want to make Chile attractive again. And we are doing it together," Quiroz said. He continued, "We may have some differences within Chile, but we are united in our purpose to bring growth, prosperity, and progress back to the country."
Quiroz said that investment is crucial for achieving higher growth rates and set a target for returning to four percent growth. "We want to get back to 4%. That is our goal. And we are here to make that transformation happen," he said.
The government’s roadmap is based on three pillars: regulatory streamlining, tax competitiveness, and fiscal consolidation. Within this framework, Quiroz described the Capital Market and Home Financing Reform Bill as central to their efforts. Using an analogy, he stated: "The capital market used to be a large aquarium, full of water and many players," referencing how pension fund withdrawals and rising public debt had diminished its depth. "This reform is about bringing more water back into it, to restore the aquarium," he said.
Addressing investors in London, Quiroz emphasized integration with global financial markets: "We need rules similar to those in the rest of the world." He also discussed making Chile's local market more appealing for companies and investors: "We need to be attractive enough for a company that left to want to come back." He added that greater financial depth could help position Chile as a regional financial hub.
Quiroz pointed out recent signs of increased investment activity: during the first six months of his government, 167 projects worth USD 34 billion were approved by the Environmental Impact Assessment System while another 144 initiatives worth USD 39 billion were submitted over the same period. Looking ahead, he stated: "We expect investment to grow 8.1% in 2027. And this figure matters... Because it's the number we need." In addition to his speech at Chile Day London 2026, Quiroz met with investors and representatives from banks and regulatory authorities regarding investment opportunities available in Chile.
